challenges.title: Hygiene chair no-shows
challenges.description: Late cancellations leave hygiene chairs empty several times a day.
challenges.reasoning: Reviews mention waiting weeks to rebook, which signals a full schedule with poor backfill; with a new six-chair clinic opened in April, unfilled slots now multiply across two locations, so lost visits are likely material.

challenges.title: Unconverted treatment plans
challenges.description: Accepted Invisalign plans are not scheduled promptly.
challenges.reasoning: Invisalign is a core high-ticket service, yet the site has no follow-up tooling and the front desk is stretched by phone volume, so pending plans likely go cold before patients book the first appointment.
signals: Invisalign listed as a core service

challenges.title: Unanswered calls at peak hours
challenges.description: Patients cannot reach the front desk during busy periods.
challenges.reasoning: Several reviews explicitly say the phone was not answered, and the same small front-desk team now covers two clinics plus insurance verification calls, so peak-hour call abandonment is the most likely cause of those reviews.
signals: Front desk also verifies insurance by phone
challenges.business_impact: Missed new-patient bookings and lower ratings

challenges.title: Manual insurance verification
challenges.description: Staff verify benefits by phone for each visit.
challenges.reasoning: The practice is in-network with 12 PPO plans and is inferred from industry norms to verify benefits manually by phone, which consumes front-desk hours that are already short because of the call volume described in reviews.

challenges.title: Thin referral engine
challenges.description: No structured referral or review-request program.
challenges.reasoning: Growth depends on local reputation as the practice expands into Cedar Park, yet no review or referral tooling appears in the tech stack, which suggests happy patients are not systematically asked to refer or review.
